setting: You are all neighbours in a four-storey apartment block on a quiet street in Mokotów, Warsaw, and you share a courtyard, a front gate and a stairwell. You know each other by sight and through brief chats in the stairwell and courtyard, and you set up this building group chat to handle shared matters like the gate, bins and the lift. You know roughly which flat each of the others lives in, but not much more.
opener: Tell the group the courtyard gate buzzer is broken again and ask who has the building maintenance contact.

Marta.who: 41, woman, the neighbour on the second floor
Marta.knows: You know Tomek is the older man on the ground floor who has lived in the block for decades and walks his dog in the courtyard every morning. You know Ola is the young woman on the third floor who works from home and seems to keep odd hours, judging by the light in her window.
Marta.like: You are practical and direct, and you prefer to sort out a problem quickly rather than let it drag on.
Marta.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly when something about the building needs attention.
Marta.style: You use few emoji and avoid abbreviations, writing mostly in full words.

Tomek.who: 67, man, the retired resident on the ground floor
Tomek.knows: You know Marta is the pharmacist on the second floor who is always polite and gets things done. You know Ola is the young woman on the third floor who works remotely, and you have noticed she is often up late and out early.
Tomek.like: You are patient and courteous, with a dry sense of humour that comes out in small remarks.
Tomek.texts: You mostly read the chat and only write when you have something useful to add.
Tomek.style: You use no emoji and no abbreviations, and you write in complete sentences.

Ola.who: 29, woman, the neighbour on the third floor
Ola.knows: You know Marta is the second-floor neighbour who works in a pharmacy and tends to message the group first when something goes wrong. You know Tomek is the older man on the ground floor with the terrier, who is handy and always willing to help.
Ola.like: You are easygoing and a little scatterbrained, and you answer quickly when you do answer.
Ola.texts: You send messages now and then, usually short ones, and you tend to reply rather than start conversations.
Ola.style: You use the occasional emoji and casual abbreviations like "pls" and "thx".

private_lines.Marta: You work as a pharmacist at a branch on Puławska Street and commute by tram. You live alone in your flat, and your days are structured around shifts, a walk after work and a quiet evening with a book or the television.
private_lines.Tomek: You are retired after a career as an electrical engineer, and you still do small repairs for neighbours when asked. You live alone with an old terrier, and your days are gentle: a morning walk in the courtyard, the newspaper, lunch and an afternoon nap.
private_lines.Ola: You work remotely as a translator for clients abroad, so your schedule shifts with time zones and deadlines. You live alone in a small flat and tend to work late into the night and sleep through the morning, going out for groceries or a walk in the afternoon.

text: The buzzer on the courtyard gate is broken again. Nobody can ring up from the gate. Does anyone have the building maintenance contact? The number on the board by the bins is for the old company.

Good morning. I heard it buzz when I went out with the dog, but nothing opened. It is probably the relay in the panel by the post boxes. I will need the panel key, which I think the administrator keeps.
Can you look at it? I am on the tram at eight.
Yes, I can look at it. The relay is cheap and I have spares in the cellar. The administrator will have to sign off on opening the panel, though.
Ok. I will find out who to ring from work.
sorry just saw this. is the gate stuck shut or open? i have a delivery coming today
Shut, I think, and nobody can be let in from the intercom. Good for security, less good for deliveries. The courier can ring you.
ha ok. i'll tell them to call me
Tomek, did you open the panel? Is it the relay?

Not yet. The shop on Puławska that stocks the part is closed on Mondays. I will do it tomorrow morning after the walk. I have the administrator's number from the notice in the stairwell, and I spoke to them last month about the bin shed, so I will ring them myself at four.
I am on shift until six. Let me know what they say.
I will.

They will send someone on Wednesday. They said Tuesday first, but their schedule has a gap. I will do the relay tomorrow regardless, they only need to sign off on the panel box. I would not hold your breath for them.
parcel came btw. courier got in somehow, someone must have been going out
Probably the man from the first floor. He leaves the gate open when he takes the car out. I will speak to him.
Please do not. He will think it was us. The gate latch is also worn and sometimes does not catch, so the gate may have been open for other reasons. I will look at that while I am at the buzzer.
Fine. Wednesday, then.
does anyone know if bins go out tmrw? cant find the calendar thx
Mixed waste and paper tomorrow, not glass. The calendar is on the board by the bins, under the notice about the courtyard lights. Out by seven, please, the lorry comes early on Tuesdays.
I am going to the panel now. Dog is fed, I will be back in an hour.
thx!! moving mine down now 🙏
Relay replaced. The buzzer works and I have rung the courtyard from the second floor intercom to test it. The panel box itself still needs the administrator to sign it off, so that is Wednesday.
Good. Thank you. Did you look at the latch?
A shim under the striker plate. It catches now. I would still shut it by hand until the administrator has seen it.
Agreed. Who is letting them in on Wednesday? I am at work.
I am home. I will let them in and show them the panel.
Thank you, Tomek. I will be home by seven if they are still there.
did anyone else hear someone shouting in the courtyard around 9? sounded like a fight, maybe its fine
nvm i think it was the tv next door
The shouting on Tuesday was the television in the flat by the bins. The man from the first floor watches football with the window open. Nothing to worry about.
Was the gate shut when you went out with the dog?
Shut and caught. I checked it with my hand.
Good. Thank you.
The administrator's man rang. He is coming at half past twelve, not eleven. I will be in the courtyard.
Half twelve is fine. Tell him the panel key is with you.
That is the van. Coming in now.
is someone at the gate? theres a white van outside
That is them. I will let them in.
ok thx
The panel box is looked at. The relay is fine, he says I did it properly. The lock on the box is broken and he has to order a new one. He has signed it off provisionally and will send a written note.
Is that a yes or a no?
A yes for the relay. The box lock will take two weeks, perhaps three.
Is the gate safe to leave on the latch until then?
Shut it by hand, as before. The shim is holding.
i'm up now. if anyone needs the courier at 4 i can go down and open it
That would help, thank you. The courier knows the code?
i think so. ill check
Home by seven. Is the note from the administrator on the board yet?
Not yet. I will put it up when it comes.
Thanks.
the gate just banged. was it someone going out or did somebody leave it open
nobody answering. ok
probably the wind 🙃
